chapter: Family band and learning to play
title: His mother's records and learning solos by slowing the turntable
summary: His mother had Bing Crosby, Bessie Smith and Gene Austin records; he learned solos and harmony by playing records slowly.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Now your mother had a record player, too.
We had a record player, too, and she --
What kind of stuff did she have?

Well, she had some things by Bing Crosby, Bessie Smith -- she had all of Bessie Smith's records -- and she had more records by vocalists than she did bands. She had Dixie Lee, that was Bing's wife, you know.

Yeah, she was big before Bing and I think she gave up her career to have babies and you know, like become a housewife and she just dropped everything. I'm pretty sure, because I remember -- and Gene Austin.
Lou Armstrong? That's the first place I heard Louie do 'West End Blues' was over to this house.
But your mother didn't have him.

No, she didn't have Louie. So whoever had the bands, that's where we'd visit more, you know, because -- then I finally started buying some records by the bands, you know, and we'd turn them all down. Then you'd wind it up and you'd set your tempo where you wanted to, you know, where you wanted it to be and that's why I could learn the solos. I could learn the solos from the record because I could play it so slow and you had to learn it, you know what I mean? And I learned how to write harmony from that, just listening and listening and putting it in there and I learned how to write harmony from listening to the records, turning it down. Man, we put it so slow.
